_comment: Record of which creator accounts have been scraped for the QA caption corpus, with the exact actor + input used. READ THIS BEFORE SCRAPING — a fresh container has no other memory of what has already been pulled, and re-scraping costs Apify credits. Captions themselves live in the `corpus` file named by each scan below, keyed by the same handle. This is research input for the QA harness only: nothing here is written to brand_voices, and it is not a DNA build.

notes: maxResultsShorts MUST equal maxResults. Setting it to 0 returns nothing at all for shorts-first creators, which looks identical to a wrong handle.
profileSorting enum is lowercase: latest | popular | oldest. Capitalized values are rejected.
profiles takes bare handles, no @ and no URL.
Date and popularity filters are separately charged add-ons; leave them unset.

accounts.warning: NOT @CarterPCs. That handle resolves to an unrelated channel named "five" (146 subscribers, 3 videos) whose own titles credit @actuallycarterpcs.
@justicebuys (no trailing 1) returns CHANNEL_DOES_NOT_EXIST. justicebuys1 is the corrected handle and was confirmed against the returned channel name and subscriber count.

accounts.note: One returned post had an empty caption and was dropped, so 49 rather than 50.

scans.note: Builder / business-idea / product-affiliate creators. Three of the nine return captions with little or no extractable substance; that is a property of the CHANNEL, not a scrape failure, and is recorded per account below so a later run does not re-scrape hoping for more.

accounts.thin: Smallest channel in either cohort at 225 subscribers, and nearly every caption is a near-duplicate promo line for one product (#buildpad) or a bare reaction fragment ("wow…", "oh my…"). 50 shorts deduplicated to 39. Expect close to zero extractable knowledge; that is the honest reading of this channel.
Captions are reach-hashtag strings with a generic opener ("Wonderful Gadgets #fyp #growmyaccount …"). Only a handful name an actual product. Low substance by construction.

accounts.note: One post had an empty caption and was dropped, so 49 rather than 50.
Captions are translated from Russian by the platform and read as one-line business-idea summaries. Two are single words ("cool", "wow").
